objects.original: For each i, the paper takes the unscaled standard Gaussian row γᵢ=((g₁)ᵢ,…,(gᵣ)ᵢ) with r=q+1, the radial square Rᵢ=‖γᵢ‖², and the weight exp(Rᵢ/3). The strict one-row application concerns the same law and radial variable.
objects.reconstructed: For E the decoder takes its canonical standard Gaussian γ_E and the real function x ↦ exp(‖x‖²/3), using the inner-product norm.
objects.evidence: A3.SS2.p1.2, A3.Ex85.m1 and A3.SS2.p10.m2–m3 identify the row law and radial variable. stdGaussian is the orthonormal synthesis of independent standard scalar Gaussians and agrees with N(0,Iᵣ) on the Euclidean carrier. The private application sets that carrier and measure at lines 19–30. The scaled tensor row of B is a distinct object.

domains.original: The radial variable lives on the Euclidean Gaussian row space ℝʳ, with positive r=q+1 and with the usual Borel probability law.
domains.reconstructed: Every finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure is allowed. Dimension zero is included and gives δ₀.
domains.evidence: A3.SS2.p1 and S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.1 supply the source dimension and law. Producer lines 21–26 allow arbitrary finite real dimension, and consumer lines 21–23 instantiate EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q+1)). Orthonormal coordinates preserve the norm and standard Gaussian law. The zero-dimensional finite product is a unit mass on zero and its moment equals 1.

quantifiers.original: Under natural d,q with 2q+1<d and the stated Gaussian row setup, the moment and the specialized tail apply to each 1≤i≤d. The excerpt uses tilt 1/3. Ex104 separately displays the tail for real x≥0, from which the cutoff instance follows.
quantifiers.reconstructed: The moment is universal over the finite-dimensional real inner-product carrier E and fixed at coefficient 1/3. Its dimension is determined by E and the standard law is canonical.
quantifiers.evidence: The exact producer and decoder both quantify over E at a fixed tilt. A3.SS2.p1.2 supplies one standard marginal for every i. The private consumer lines 19–24 retains the natural d,q binders and the source range and supplies the x=log(1000d) instance for this marginal. The arbitrary-x chain is a residual of the broader source paragraph.

assumptions.original: The source has independent N(0,I_d) starts, hence each row has independent standard scalar coordinates and the rows are jointly independent. The cutoff application has q≥0 and 2q+1<d. The moment uses only the standard marginal law.
assumptions.reconstructed: E carries its finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel structures, and integration uses the concrete standard Gaussian probability measure. No moment, integrability or tail bound is assumed.
assumptions.evidence: The standard marginal law in A3.SS2.p1.2 is fixed by the concrete stdGaussian definition, whose finite product includes coordinate independence. The producer carrier binders are typing information. The consumer premise 2q+1<d supplies d>0. Producer lines 78–98 prove integrability and the consumer lines 36–44 and 79–82 use it.

conclusion.original: The finite expectation E exp(Rᵢ/3)=3^(r/2) is asserted at p10.m3. At L=2r+3 log(1000d), Ex104 gives the strict single-row tail P(Rᵢ>L)≤1/(1000d).
conclusion.reconstructed: The decoder states integrability and the real Bochner integral equal to 3^(dimℝ E/2). Its reconstruction is of the public moment declaration.
conclusion.evidence: The decoder matches both producer conjuncts at lines 21–26. The finite lower integral and conversion at lines 78–98 supply the source's ordinary finite expectation. The exact private statement and proof at lines 19–82 separately give the cutoff conclusion using both producer conjuncts.

scopes.original: Expectation is for the standard marginal of the unscaled row. The bad event Rᵢ>L is strict, so equality belongs to the retained event. The all-row event Ex105 and its p10.3 probability follow by a separate finite union bound.
scopes.reconstructed: The decoder treats the integral as the genuine real Bochner integral with integrability under a normalized standard Gaussian. Its statement is the radial moment.
scopes.evidence: Producer lines 91–98 discharge integrability before the real integral comparison. Consumer lines 67–82 preserve the strict event and use a weak Markov event as a superset only. The lesson labels the private one-row application. The correspondence cites p10.3 for the downstream context and explicitly stops before transfer to the row family and finite union bound.

constant_dependencies.original: The tilt is exactly 1/3, the moment is 3 raised to real r/2, and the threshold and budget use the absolute factors 2, 3 and 1000 in L=2r+3 log(1000d) and 1/(1000d). The norm carries no d-dependent scaling.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The decoder preserves the fixed coefficient 1/3, base 3 and real exponent dimℝ(E)/2. The public moment has no d or q parameter.
constant_dependencies.evidence: A3.SS2.p10.m1–m3 and A3.Ex104.m1 give the constants. Producer lines 27–29 and 54–69 and the exact typed Real.rpow bind the real half-dimension. Consumer lines 27–35 and 46–65 specialize r=q+1 and keep the literal cutoff and reciprocal; no tensor scaling or cosine coefficient enters.

deltas.description: The public theorem extends the Euclidean row moment to any finite-dimensional real inner-product carrier, including dimension zero.

deltas.evidence: A3.SS2.p10.m3 and Ex104 use a finite exponential moment. Producer lines 78–98 prove it before passing from the lower integral to the real integral.
